question: Should OpenClaw core own this versioned aggregate recovery-point contract and validate a runtime-state inventory receipt, or should the aggregate lifecycle identity remain entirely host-owned until a smaller core seam is agreed?
rationale: The implementation is intentionally private and mechanically bounded, but choosing its permanent owner sets a compatibility-sensitive recovery and session-state contract that code review cannot determine from correctness alone.

options.title: Accept the private core seam
options.body: Approve the aggregate verifier/composer as a core primitive, with the runtime-state owner explicitly defining the activation-pinned inventory producer before merge.

options.title: Reduce to existing snapshot primitives
options.body: Keep the existing owner-scoped SQLite snapshot API and move aggregate identity, obligations, and host orchestration to the external host until a new core API is justified.

options.title: Pause pending RFC decision
options.body: Leave this PR unmerged while the RFC establishes the ownership and portability contract shared by the stacked recovery work.

recommendation.title: Accept the private core seam
recommendation.body: Approve the aggregate verifier/composer as a core primitive, with the runtime-state owner explicitly defining the activation-pinned inventory producer before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The proposed composition is layered directly over the existing SQLite snapshot primitive identified in the PR context.
